# <a id="_id3t93xihlzo"></a>__The Curious Case of the Treed Cat: A 1970s Suburban Saga__

[JANET RILEY](https://substack.com/@juanita4141)

Jan 18, 2026

![](data:image/jpeg;base64,)

In the cozy, half\-moon embrace of our Northern Virginia townhouses back in the 1970s, nestled around a green park thick with trees, life had a certain predictable rhythm\. That is, until the cat decided to introduce a new, decidedly un\-rhythmic howl to the suburban soundtrack\. This wasn’t just *any* cat; this was a seasoned traveler, having moved around the country with us, a feline veteran of many postal codes\.

One evening, my sister arrived home from school to find him perched precariously in the upper branches of a towering oak, caterwauling with the kind of desperate fervor usually reserved for operatic villains\. A full\-blown “hissy fit” from my sister ensued, complete with dramatic tears\. My mother, ever the pragmatic peacekeeper, sighed and, to my sister’s immense relief, agreed to call a professional tree climber\. It wasn’t cheap, but for the sake of peace and a silent night, the cat was eventually rescued, blinking in the unfamiliar ground\-level light\.

Peace, however, was a fleeting visitor\. A mere couple of days later, the seasoned traveler was back in a different tree, once again serenading the neighborhood with his distressed howls\. My sister, predictably, became distraught\. But this time, Mom’s patience had worn thin\. “No,” she declared, with the finality of a judge\. “I am not paying another penny to rescue that cat\. He needs to learn his lesson\.”

And learn his lesson he did, or so Mom hoped\. For two nights, the neighborhood was subjected to an incessant, mournful serenade\. Sleep became a luxury, and the collective frustration of the townhouses grew\. Soon, the phone lines to the local fire department began to light up\. Neighbors, tired of the nightly wails, were demanding action\. It felt like something straight out of an old “Andy Griffith Show”—a small\-town crisis requiring uniformed heroes\.

Sure enough, a bright red fire truck, sirens silent but presence undeniable, pulled up to the curb, drawing a crowd of eager spectators from every townhouse\. This was better than prime\-time TV\. The firefighters, looking a bit bewildered by the feline culprit, extended their ladder\. But, in a comical twist, it wasn’t quite long enough to reach the branch where the defiant cat held court\.

Then came the fateful suggestion: “We could try knocking him out with water\.” My sister went ballistic\. “No way\!” she shrieked, envisioning a soggy, traumatized furball plummeting to its doom\. The crowd murmured\. The firefighters shrugged\. The cat continued his pitiful cries\.

In a moment of desperation, my sister cornered her then\-boyfriend\. He, bless his heart, found a ladder that *was* long enough, grabbed a can of tuna, and, like a suburban knight, ascended the tree\. With the promise of fishy goodness, he coaxed the stubborn feline down to safety\.

The cat, having caused a two\-day neighborhood siege and a fire department call\-out, finally learned his lesson\. Whether it was the indignity of the spectacle, a harrowing encounter with a squirrel, or just a deep reflection on his life choices, he never climbed another tree again\. The park, once his vertical playground, became simply a place for ground\-level contemplation\. And the suburban legend of the cat who called in the fire department was born\.
